title: Cognizant forms OpenAI delivery group for code, legacy systems and customer operations
summary: Cognizant’s new OpenAI practice covers Codex, legacy modernization and customer operations. Its staffing commitment differs from proven client delivery.

# Cognizant forms OpenAI delivery group for code, legacy systems and customer operations


By OpenTools Team


The October 30 practice announcement brings together more than 25,000 professionals. Its three initial workstreams include modernization with consequential engineering review.


##


Three initial delivery workstreams


Cognizant[formed its OpenAI Frontier Capability Group on October 30](https://en.prnasia.com/releases/apac/cognizant-commits-more-than-25-000-professionals-to-openai-delivery-as-enterprises-move-frontier-ai-into-production-553976.shtml) , bringing together more than 25,000 professionals to deliver OpenAI products for clients. Its initial scope covers:


- **Software engineering**


Codex‑assisted development.


- **Application modernization**


Legacy mainframe analysis through cloud‑native code generation, using Cognizant Application Modernizer powered by OpenAI models.


- **Customer operations**


Sales, service and support.


##


Modernization retains consequential engineering review


The[announcement](https://en.prnasia.com/releases/apac/cognizant-commits-more-than-25-000-professionals-to-openai-delivery-as-enterprises-move-frontier-ai-into-production-553976.shtml) says engineers review every consequential decision in the modernization workflow. It also says Cognizant already uses an OpenAI‑based solution in its own sales and customer‑success operations.


For a team commissioning a legacy‑system migration, this makes the scope of a proposal consequential. A request to explain an existing program is different from a request to replace it. A useful work order identifies the input system, the behavior to preserve and who accepts the replacement. Generating code is one step in that handoff.


The[agent‑skills engineering guide](https://opentools.ai/resources/agent-skills) describes specification, testing and review gates for coding agents. It offers a vocabulary for defining acceptance, rather than evidence about Cognizant’s internal process.


##


A delivery‑group headcount is not a customer outcome


The announced organization is a commitment of people to a practice; it does not report 25,000 new hires, a particular customer’s staffing allocation or an independently measured delivery result. Buyers still need the scope and acceptance evidence for their own work.


OpenTools’[coverage of Cognizant’s earlier code‑assistance disclosure](https://opentools.ai/news/cognizant-q3-ai-assisted-code-credentials-revenue-measurement) examines a different question: what the company’s adoption and credential counts measure. The new practice announcement identifies the work it intends to deliver; it does not turn those earlier measures into proof of client performance.
